instagram.caption:
Never get AI slop again, here's how! 👇

Do you ask AI to write something for you, only for it to come back with that slightly artificial twist? Or worse, the dreaded em dash. You know what I'm talking about 😂

As a business owner, I want everything in my marketing to meet the same standard, and that includes what AI writes. So I taught it what's acceptable: how I talk, the words I love and the phrases I'd never use.

It's a one-time setup, and it keeps learning as you go. During setup it can even look back through your past chats for things you forgot to mention.

Check out scrollyseo.com to copy my homework and build your own Scrolly Business Brain.

instagram.caption:
25 ready-to-film Reel ideas land every week in the $1K Challenge, link in bio. These numbers come from Socialinsider's look at 6 million Reels posted by brands from January to June 2026. "Median" means the middle Reel in each length group, so one viral video can't skew the number. A good way to use this: pick the length that fits the job. Explaining a process or showing a before and after? Give it 45 to 60 seconds. Testing a new hook or format? A short Reel gets you an answer faster.

instagram.caption:
Your $1K number and a plan for each week are in the $1K Challenge, link in bio. Want to check the math yourself first? Here's where the 2.5% comes from: Littledata's study of 421 Shopify stores found a median of 1.4% of visits ending in a sale, and Dynamic Yield's data from 400+ brands averages 2.66%. One clear offer shown to people who already watched your videos can reasonably aim near 2.5%, but plan with the lower number too. One more thing: Instagram counts replays as views, so views are always higher than the number of people.

#smallbusinesstips #instagramforbusiness #onlinebusiness

ideas.title: Reel: How many views does $1,000 take?
ideas.hook: On screen (first second, top of the 3:4 band): How many views does $1,000 take? / (read the caption)
ideas.cta: Free Income Goal calculator (scrollyseo.com/calculators/income-goal/ (http://scrollyseo.com/calculators/income-goal/))
ideas.notes: Drafted by Claude 2026-10-08 from Playbook $1K math. Mercedes to confirm she's OK with the free calculator as the CTA.

instagram.caption:
Your $1,000 goal tells you how many views you need, and the free Income Goal calculator on scrollyseo.com (http://scrollyseo.com) works it out for you. Here's the math it does:

1. $1,000 ÷ your average order value = the sales you need
2. Sales ÷ the % of website visitors who buy = the visitors you need
3. Visitors ÷ the % of viewers who click through to your site = the views you need

That last number is your target for the month. Plan your posts around it.

ideas.title: Reel: 1 Reel idea = 3 Trial Reels
ideas.hook: On screen (first second): 1 Reel idea = 3 Trial Reels / (read the caption)
ideas.cta: $1K Club Playbook
ideas.notes: Drafted by Claude 2026-10-08 from Playbook ch. 9 (Trial Reel routine; Instagram help is the source there).

instagram.caption:
Post every new Reel idea as three Trial Reels, then share only the winner to your feed. The full routine is in the $1K Club Playbook. Here's how it works:

1. Version 1: the Reel as you first made it.
2. A new hook: same Reel, different opening line and first frame.
3. A bigger edit: a different first clip, a new order, a tighter cut, or a different format.
4. After 24 hours, compare views, shares, and comments.
5. Open the best one's insights and tap Share to everyone.

Trial Reels go to people who don't follow you yet, so each one is a free test.

ideas.title: Reel: Your first 3 seconds
ideas.hook: On screen (first second): 3 ways to stop the scroll in your first 3 seconds / (read the caption)
ideas.cta: $1K Club Playbook
ideas.notes: Drafted by Claude 2026-10-08 from Playbook ch. 9. Parked: Mercedes says a reel about visual hooks must itself open on a real visual hook, and the current b-roll doesn't. Needs new footage first.

instagram.caption:
Your Reel insights show a skip rate: the share of viewers who swiped away in the first 3 seconds. The $1K Club Playbook covers how to read it. Three ways to keep that number down:

1. Start on the subject. Your product, your work, or your face, in the very first frame.
2. Put the hook on screen in the first second, in your buyer's words.
3. Give the eyes something to notice: movement, a close-up, or an unusual angle.
